stories.headline: War on drugs: J&K ranks 1st in PIT-NDPS detentions, 3rd in property attachments
stories.title: War on drugs: J&K ranks 1st in PIT-NDPS detentions, 3rd in property attachments
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir has emerged as one of the leading regions in the country in enforcement against the drug trade, ranking first in detentions under the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PIT-NDPS) Act and third in property attachments. According to official figures presented as part of the administration’s drug de-addiction measures during a recent meeting convened by members of the NITI Aayog, 3,072 cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act have been registered in Jammu and Kashmir since January 1, 2026. The cases have resulted in 3,556 arrests and 376 convictions. The authorities have also attached 421 properties valued at Rs 196 crore and detained 169 persons under the PIT-NDPS Act. As part of regulatory and enforcement action against the drug network, 160 drug hotspots have been identified, while 1,698 suspects are currently under surveillance, the official figures show. Authorities have also cancelled 22 drug-store licences and suspended 400 licences as part of measures to prevent the diversion and misuse of controlled substances. The government has simultaneously intensified its crackdown on the illicit cultivation of narcotic crops. During the period, 12 acres of poppy and 144 acres of cannabis cultivation were destroyed. A total of 247 cases were registered in connection with such cultivation, leading to the arrest of 254 persons. The official data states that illegal poppy cultivation has been “nearly eliminated”. The enforcement drive has also extended to transport-related documents. Authorities have suspended 781 vehicle registrations and 669 driving licences in connection with drug-related cases. The administration has issued a common Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) governing the cancellation or suspension of documents and facilities of persons accused under the NDPS Act and those detained under the PIT-NDPS Act. The SOP covers passports, driving licences, arms licences, contractor licences, government accommodation and security. According to the framework, the objective is to restrict the mobility of accused persons, prevent misuse of identity and disrupt drug networks. “Trigger events for initiating action include an FIR involving commercial quantity, detention orders, court orders, intelligence inputs and conviction,” the official document states. Under the procedure, the investigating officer is required to prepare a case dossier containing the accused person’s identity details, relevant documents and particulars of the offence. A Look Out Circular (LOC) is then issued to prevent foreign travel. The SOP provides for cancellation or suspension of documents and facilities, including passports, driving licences, arms licences, security and government accommodation. Post-conviction measures are to ensure continuation of the cancellation or suspension and the LOC, as applicable. In cases of acquittal, the framework provides for restoration of documents and rights, withdrawal of the LOC and unfreezing of accounts. The SOP also calls for coordinated monitoring through clearly defined roles, timelines, nodal officers and mechanisms for reporting and review. Alongside enforcement, the government has reported a substantial expansion of treatment and counselling services for people affected by substance abuse. Since January 2026, treatment has been provided to 5,321 new out-patient department (OPD) cases and 801 new in-patient department (IPD) cases. The facilities have also recorded 1.79 lakh follow-up visits. The official figures show that 799 patients were discharged, while 15,054 patients received counselling. The government has also said that awareness campaigns were conducted across all panchayats through rallies, seminars and workshops.

stories.title: India sends fifth aircraft to Nepal with rescue team, medicines as flood aid expands

article_sentences: India has sent its fifth aircraft to Nepal carrying an 11-member rescue team and 5.5 tonnes of medicines as flood relief and recovery efforts expand.

India has dispatched its fifth aircraft to flood-hit Nepal, carrying an 11-member rescue team, specialised equipment and 5.5 tonnes of essential medicines, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Wednesday.

The latest deployment comes as India expands its humanitarian, medical and technical assistance to Nepal following the devastating August 26 floods in the Bhotekoshi River area of Rasuwa, which caused widespread destruction and disrupted key transport and communication links.
The fifth aircraft adds to a growing Indian relief operation that has moved beyond emergency supplies to include specialised rescue capabilities and infrastructure support.
India has already airlifted 68.5 tonnes of relief material to Kathmandu.
The supplies include essential medicines, food packets, portable generators, water purification tablets, shelter materials and heavy technical equipment.
On Sunday, India sent its fourth relief flight carrying 11 tonnes of essential supplies and specialised personnel to assist Nepal's rescue and recovery operations.
The shipment included blankets, sleeping bags, tarpaulins, plastic sheets and hygiene kits.
Specialised equipment and personnel for complex tunnel search-and-rescue operations were also deployed.
A team of forensic experts equipped with specialised tools for DNA analysis has also arrived in Nepal to support authorities in victim identification and forensic assessments.
India's assistance is also focused on restoring connectivity in areas where infrastructure has been severely affected by the floods.
Jaishankar had earlier said that 16 trucks carrying equipment for a 230-foot Single Lane Modular Steel Bridge had reached Nepal.

stories.headline: High Court dismisses plea questioning Shopian Bar Association’s election rules
stories.title: High Court dismisses plea questioning Shopian Bar Association’s election rules
stories.summary: The High Court of J&K and Ladakh has rejected a plea challenging the amended Constitution of the District Bar Association Shopian. Dismissing an advocate’s plea challenging the 2023 amendment enhancing the eligibility criteria for contesting the posts of President, Vice-President and Secretary of the Association, a bench of Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal held that disputes concerning the lawyers’ body’s internal affairs and elections are not amenable to writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution. Under the amended provisions, the required standing at the Bar was increased from 10 to 15 years for President and Vice-President and from seven to 10 years for Secretary. The petitioner had called into question the election notification issued on December 11, 2025, contending that the amendment had been introduced without following due procedure. He further contended that no valid General Body Meeting was held, no proper notice was circulated and no resolution approving the amendment had been passed. The amendment, he argued, was arbitrary and intended to exclude younger advocates from contesting elections. Opposing the plea, the respondents said that the amendment had been approved by the General Body after due notice and a majority vote. The Association, they said, was a voluntary body governed by its own Constitution and bye-laws and was neither “State” under Article 12 nor a body performing a public function under Article 226. Agreeing with the respondents’ preliminary objection, the court held that the District Bar Association Shopian neither derives its existence from any statute nor exercises statutory powers or governmental functions. It observed that merely because its members are advocates and the legal profession has an important role in the administration of justice, every activity of the Association cannot be treated as a public function. The Court underscored that the dispute over eligibility for holding office in the Association concerned internal governance and the electoral rights of its members, without any public-law element. It therefore could not be examined through writ jurisdiction. The Court noted that the case involved disputed questions of fact, including whether notice for the General Body Meeting was issued, whether the meeting was held and whether the amendment was validly approved. Such issues require examination of evidence and are more appropriately adjudicated by a competent civil court, it said. Moreover, the Court took note of the delay in challenging the 2023 amendment. “The amended Constitution had remained operative for a considerable period and subsequent elections had allegedly been conducted under it.” The Court observed that the petitioner’s conduct raised issues of acquiescence and approbation and reprobation, particularly as the challenge was made after the issuance of the election notification when the amended eligibility criteria affected his candidature. The Court, in keeping with the Supreme Court and various High Court decisions, including a recent one concerning the New Delhi Bar Association, reiterated that a Bar Association does not become amenable to writ jurisdiction merely because it consists of advocates. The Court accordingly dismissed the petition as “not maintainable”.

stories.headline: US and Iran trade strikes, and other Mideast news
stories.title: US and Iran trade strikes, and other Mideast news
stories.summary: Dubai, Sep 02: The United States military struck targets in Iran on Tuesday as hostilities flared after a month without military action. Iran fired missiles and drones in response, Iranian semiofficial media said. The Fars and Tasnim news agencies, seen as close to Iran's security forces, reported late Tuesday that Iran had launched such operations. One US strike hit a home hosting a wedding, killing five people and wounding dozens, local officials said. Here's a look at the latest developments in the Iran war and the wider Middle East. Full coverage can be found here. US strikes targets in Iran US Central Command said the new strikes come after Tehran tried to attack commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and US service members in the region. US President Donald Trump warned in a social media post that if Iran retaliates, “they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings.” On Sunday, the US military said it struck rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran responded by launching missiles at US sites in Jordan, which were intercepted, while the United Arab Emirates said it stopped an Iranian drone over its waters. After the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, Iran established a chokehold on the strait, through which a fifth of the world's traded oil passed in peacetime, slowing ship traffic to a trickle. That has roiled the global economy, raising prices worldwide for energy and other goods. While Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian has long favoured a negotiated end to the war, the most powerful force in Iran remains the paramilitary Revolutionary Guard, which is pressing for greater concessions from the US, including Iranian control over the strait and financial compensation for the war. Those conditions would likely be unacceptable to Washington. US renews regionwide Mideast travel alert The State Department renewed a regionwide travel alert for the Middle East as hostilities between the US and Iran resumed. “Due to tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation,” the department said in a blanket advisory covering all countries in the region. The language is similar to that used in previous warnings that came before a lull in combat activities and said Americans in the Mideast should exercise heightened vigilance and be aware of potential travel disruptions. Iran is working with Oman on a plan for shipping traffic Iran has been working with Oman, which sits on the south side of the Strait of Hormuz, on a framework for managing shipping traffic, though it remains unclear whether the plan would be acceptable to the US. Other Gulf nations have stressed the need to reopen the strait unconditionally. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the kingdom's de facto ruler, met with Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq on Tuesday, according to the Saudi Press Agency, which said the two discussed “ongoing efforts to maintain regional security and stability,” but did not mention the strait specifically. Iran continues to deny UN inspectors access to nuclear sites The United Nations nuclear watchdog has been unable to inspect nuclear facilities in Iran affected by the 12-day war in June 2025, according to a confidential report by the UN watchdog circulated to member states and seen Tuesday by The Associated Press. The International Atomic Energy Agency said in its report that therefore it “cannot provide any information on the current size, composition or whereabouts of the stockpile of enriched uranium in Iran.” Israeli raid to detain Hamas militant in Gaza kills 4 people Israel said it detained a senior Hamas security official in a special forces raid in Gaza City on Tuesday. The operation killed at least four people, including two children, hospital officials said. In a joint statement, Israel's military and national security agency said the operation targeted the head of Hamas' internal security. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement that the detainee, who he did not name, is “one of the most senior Hamas leaders” and that he was most recently “engaged in efforts to restore Hamas's governance in Gaza.” Islamic State spokesperson killed in Yemen Yemen's state security said that Islamic State spokesperson Abu Huzayfah al-Ansari was killed in Yemen in a joint operation by Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and the Yemeni counterterrorism forces. He was killed at dawn Tuesday while he was hiding in a house in Seiyun city in the Yemeni province of Hadramout, according to a security statement published by state-run SABA news agency. A US official, who was not authorised to comment publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity, said there was no US military involvement in the operation. (AP) 2 ships attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz The British military's United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre said it received reports of an attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, and a second report involving a nearby tanker. The UKMTO said a tanker was hit by three projectiles Monday on its way out of the Persian Gulf through the strait east of Oman. stories.title: Nepal’s only billionaire praises India, PM Modi for swift disaster response; calls rebuilding task ‘gigantic’
stories.summary: Nepal’s only billionaire and philanthropist Binod Chaudhary on Tuesday praised India and Prime Minister Narendra Modi for their swift response to the devastating flash floods in the country, saying the scale of the disaster was “far bigger” than anyone had contemplated. Chaudhary also described the rebuilding task as “gigantic”, highlighting how villages, markets, schools and bridges were washed away and more than 500 megawatts of power generation capacity went out of operation. “The scale of the disaster is far bigger than one would have ever contemplated. We had floods in the past in the same location even last year and that’s nowhere close to what it is now,” Chaudhary told PTI Videos. “We’ve lost about a thousand people. About 4,000 people are missing... More than the last count that I’ve taken, we had lost some 40-odd bridges,” he said, highlighting the scale of damages. “More than 500 megawatts of power stations had gone out of circulation, out of operation and many projects which were under construction, particularly the power projects, they all had to be halted, they’re washed away, damaged. So it’s really a very, very painful situation,” Chaudhary added. The death toll from the devastating flash floods in Nepal crossed 1,000 on Tuesday, as rescuers struggled to trace those stranded amid intermittent rainfall and a fresh flood alert. Around 4,000 people, including 583 foreigners, remained missing, while around 12,000 people had been rescued, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Chaudhary praised the Nepal government, security agencies and friendly neighbours, particularly India, for their response to the disaster. “I must acknowledge that the government and the security agencies and also supported by our friendly neighbours, India in particular has done a great job in supporting, in coming forward with the relief material right away,” he said. He particularly praised New Delhi and PM Modi for supporting Nepal, not just after the latest disaster but also recalling India’s response during the 2015 earthquake. “I think we have no doubt in my mind that India is equally concerned. And I’ve seen this on multiple occasions. Even during the 2015 earthquake, India was the first one, Prime Minister Modi was the first one to come up with the immediate rescue arrangement, support, infrastructure, logistics,” he said. He said India had “gained that prominence, gained that capacity” and the ability to respond on a large scale. “Given the scale at which India has been able to move, build the infrastructure. There has been a transformation in the quality of the infrastructure that India has been able to build over during the last 12 years. So the whole system is of a different level and caliber,” Chaudhary said. “I would hope and I would appeal to the Indian government, Prime Minister Modi and all those who matter to do everything possible. I think these are the moments when India can make a big difference,” Chaudhary said. Chaudhary said financial assistance from different countries, companies, foundations and business houses remained of utmost importance, but cautioned that “money is one thing” and it cannot solve the problems overnight. “You can’t get the markets [to] start to function again. You can’t rebuild the homes to house these people who are homeless,” he said. Chaudhary emphasised that the task ahead was gigantic and Nepal would have to rebuild better. “It is also an engineering issue. It is not only an issue which relates with one of those normal disasters, because the glacier meltdown because of global warming is really becoming a significant issue, which the whole world should be concerned about,” he added.

stories.headline: NC, BJP to stage counter protests in Srinagar; security tightened
stories.title: NC, BJP to stage counter protests in Srinagar; security tightened
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 02: Police and security forces were deployed in large numbers at Lal Chowk and Jawahar Nagar here on Wednesday to maintain law and order in view of the BJP plan to gherao the Civil Secretariat and the ruling National Conference's plan to stage a counter protest outside the office of the national party. Roads leading to the BJP office at Jawahar Nagar have been sealed to prevent any unruly gathering, while all entry points to Ghanta Ghar at Lal Chowk have been put off limits to all vehicles, the officials said. The BJP has asked its workers to assemble at Ghanta Ghar before they march towards the Civil Secretariat across the Budshah Bridge over River Jhelum, while the National Conference has asked its workers to gather outside Gindun Sports Complex at Rajbagh for the march towards the BJP's office. While the NC will gherao the BJP headquarters in Jammu and Srinagar over statehood issue, the BJP's gherao of the Civil Secretariat here is over the Omar Abdullah government's alleged failure to fulfil its electoral promises. The NC announced that it will gherao the opposition BJP headquarters in Jammu and Srinagar, demanding accountability for the promises the Union government made in Parliament and the Supreme Court regarding the restoration of statehood. The NC's protest announcement comes in response to the BJP's secretariat gherao plan for Wednesday to protest against the alleged failure of the Omar Abdullah government to deliver on the promises made by it during the election campaign in 2024. The BJP, the principal opposition party in Jammu and Kashmir, had originally planned its secretariat gherao on July 20 but postponed it due to NC holding a peaceful sit-in at Jantar Mantar in Delhi to press for restoration of statehood to J-K. A BJP spokesperson said the youth of J-K are asking questions which the NC government must answer. "On September 2, we shall raise the concerns over alleged backdoor appointments, job outsourcing, unemployment, corruption and unfulfilled commitments outside the Civil Secretariat, Srinagar," he said. The spokesperson said the youth of Jammu and Kashmir deserve jobs and transparency in the appointments. Jammu and Kashmir was reorganised into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh in August 2019 following the abrogation of Article 370. In December 2023, the Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of the Centre's decision, observing that statehood should be restored as soon as possible.

stories.headline: PDP and the politics of deception
stories.title: PDP and the politics of deception
stories.summary: For more than two decades, the Peoples Democratic Party has attempted an extraordinary political balancing act in Jammu & Kashmir—speaking one language while exercising power and another when sitting in opposition. Its politics has repeatedly moved between constitutional mainstream, soft-separatist rhetoric, reconciliation with Pakistan and aggressive criticism of New Delhi, depending upon the political circumstances of the moment. This is not ideological consistency. It is politics of convenience. The 2014 Contradiction The clearest example remains 2014. PDP sought votes in Kashmir by positioning itself strongly against BJP. Yet after the election it entered into an alliance with the very party it had opposed and formed the Government. BJP's ideological position was never concealed. Its views on nationalism, Article 370 and complete integration of J&K with India were known for decades. PDP nevertheless shared power with BJP. If BJP was politically acceptable when ministerial offices were available, how did it suddenly become ideologically unacceptable when PDP lost power? Principles cannot change according to one's distance from the Chief Minister's chair. 2016 Exposed the Contradiction The unrest following the killing of Hizbul Mujahideen commander Burhan Wani in July 2016 provides an even more telling example. When Mehbooba Mufti was Chief Minister and responsible for maintaining law and order, her language was very different from the rhetoric PDP frequently employs from the opposition benches. In August 2016, she said a small percentage was creating havoc and questioned those attacking police stations and security camps. Later that year, she urged security forces to exercise restraint and avoid pellet guns where possible. The important point is not to reopen the tragedy of 2016. It is to ask a question of political consistency. When responsible for government, PDP understood the compulsions of maintaining public order. Outside government, why does its political narrative so frequently sound as though those compulsions never existed? Kashmir deserves honesty about this contradiction. Jamaat-e-Islami: Why This Political Priority? The contradiction continues today. In July 2026, Mehbooba Mufti said PDP would join the proposed opposition protest in Delhi only if its agenda included restoration of Article 370, release of political prisoners and lifting the ban on Jamaat-e-Islami. BJP is entitled to ask: why should lifting the ban on Jamaat become such an important political priority? Every organisation is entitled to whatever legal remedies are available to it. But political parties seeking to govern J&K must make their priorities equally clear. At a time when young Kashmiris want jobs, investment, modern universities, technology, tourism and entrepreneurship, politics should concentrate upon connecting them with India's enormous opportunities rather than constantly returning them to old ideological battlegrounds. Pakistan Again and Again PDP's 2024 manifesto once again placed considerable emphasis upon the Kashmir issue, India-Pakistan engagement, restoration of constitutional guarantees and cross-LoC economic connectivity. Dialogue between countries is ultimately a matter for the Union Government, determined by national interest and security circumstances. But Kashmir's people must ask what decades of Pakistan-centred political discourse actually delivered to their families. Did it create jobs? Did it bring industries? Did it protect tourism from instability? Did it give Kashmir's children uninterrupted education? The ordinary Kashmiri paid the greatest price whenever terrorism, street violence and instability overwhelmed normal life. The children of Kashmir need laptops, not another generation of conflict. Article 370 and Political Convenience PDP's politics around Article 370 presents another contradiction. Its 2014 manifesto called Article 370 essential and advocated using it to restore J&K's original special status. Yet PDP subsequently governed in coalition with BJP despite knowing BJP's decades-old ideological position on Article 370. Today PDP again projects restoration of constitutional guarantees as central to its politics. It is perfectly entitled to advocate its constitutional position democratically. But voters are equally entitled to ask: If these ideological differences were so fundamental, how did they become manageable while governmental power was being shared? BJP's Position Has Never Been Hidden This is where BJP offers a fundamental contrast. One may support or oppose BJP, but its position has been consistent. BJP opposed Article 370 for decades. When it acquired the parliamentary and constitutional capacity, Article 370 was rendered inoperative. There was no separate position in Jammu, another in Srinagar and a third in Delhi. Political clarity is healthier than calculated ambiguity. Kashmir's Youth Deserve Better The biggest victims of emotional politics have always been ordinary young Kashmiris. Political families survived every turmoil. Ordinary families bore the consequences. When schools closed, ordinary children lost education. When tourism collapsed, ordinary workers lost income. When markets shut, ordinary traders suffered. When violence erupted, ordinary families lived in fear. J&K cannot afford another generation trapped in grievance politics. Its youth want careers, startups, artificial intelligence, tourism, world-class infrastructure, sports, universities and opportunities across India and the world. They should not become raw material for anybody's political revival. Politics Must Move Forward PDP must decide what it ultimately wants to represent: a modern democratic party competing on development and governance, or a political formation repeatedly returning to emotionally charged issues whenever it needs to recover electoral space. Jammu & Kashmir has changed. The old political formulas cannot indefinitely be repackaged and sold to new generations. Kashmir's pain cannot become anybody's permanent political business model. People deserve consistency. They deserve accountability. Above all, they deserve leaders who say the same thing whether they are in Government or opposition. PDP's record raises a question it cannot escape: Why do its political principles appear strongest when it is out of power and most flexible when power is within reach? The people of Jammu & Kashmir have seen this politics before. They should not be deceived by it again. Advocate Sunil Sethi , Senior Advocate & Chief Spokesperson, BJP J&K.

stories.headline: The politics of an endless tomorrow
stories.title: The politics of an endless tomorrow
stories.summary: Politics has a curious relationship with unfinished promises. A promise that is fulfilled ceases to be a promise; it becomes a fact. A promise that fails, however, can acquire an unexpected political afterlife. It can be repeated, refined, mourned, blamed on circumstances, and eventually presented to the electorate once again—as though its previous failure were itself evidence of the sincerity of those who made it. In this peculiar economy of democratic politics, the unfulfilled promise can become more durable than the fulfilled one. stories.summary: The Environmental Policy Group (EPG) has sought measures for protection of water bodies in Srinagar. EPG in a statement has sought the intervention of Chief Minister Omar Abdullah over a video circulating on social media that allegedly shows filling or reclamation of a portion of Dal Lake near the office of the Lakes Conservation and Management Authority (LCMA) at Miskeen Bagh. In a letter addressed to the Chief Minister, EPG urged the competent authorities to verify the video and establish the exact location and nature of the activity shown. The group said the matter required prompt examination given the ecological importance and sensitivity of Dal Lake. EPG Convenor Faiz Ahmad Bakshi said that if the activity shown in the video involves filling of a water body, reclamation of lake area, dumping of material, alteration of a water channel or unauthorised encroachment, it could raise environmental and regulatory concerns. The group has sought a spot inspection by LCMA and other concerned departments to determine whether any portion of lake near Miskeen Bagh has been filled, reclaimed, encroached upon or otherwise altered. It has also asked the authorities to verify the ownership, land classification, revenue status and permissible land use of the area shown in the video. The EPG said the concern was not limited to Dal Lake and called for greater attention to the protection of water bodies and natural drainage systems across Jammu and Kashmir. “Jammu & Kashmir possesses a highly interconnected network of lakes, wetlands, rivers, streams, springs, nallahs, flood channels and other natural water systems,” the group said. It referred to Wular Lake, Anchar Lake, Nigeen Lake, Manasbal Lake, Khushal Sar, Gilsar and Hokersar, besides the River Jhelum and its tributaries. “These water bodies are not vacant land available for gradual reclamation,” the EPG said, adding that they play a role in water storage, regulating flows, supporting biodiversity, groundwater recharge and flood protection. The group also referred to Government of India documentation on encroachment pressures affecting the lacustrine systems of the Kashmir Valley and cited observations from the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report on the conservation and management of Dal Lake. The EPG said the CAG report had recorded issues including blocked nallahs, construction affecting drainage, dumping of construction material and shrinkage of drainage channels. The organisation has called for a comprehensive review of major lakes, wetlands, rivers, streams, springs, nallahs, flood channels and natural drainage systems across J&K to identify cases of encroachment, filling, reclamation and obstruction. It has proposed GIS- and satellite-based mapping of major water bodies and their buffer areas, followed by physical verification on the ground. The group has also suggested continuous monitoring of sensitive water bodies through satellite imagery, drone surveys, GIS mapping and periodic field inspections. The EPG further urged the government to ensure that any filling, reclamation, construction or alteration affecting the natural extent or drainage characteristics of a water body is subjected to environmental, hydrological and technical scrutiny by the competent authorities. It has also suggested treating natural flood channels, nallahs, wetlands and drainage corridors as important components of climate and disaster resilience. The group has called for greater transparency in the handling of encroachment cases and suggested that information on identified encroachments and action taken by the authorities be made publicly accessible. “Jammu & Kashmir's water bodies are part of its natural capital,” the EPG said, adding that they should be protected while development activities are undertaken. The group has requested the Chief Minister to direct the concerned authorities to examine the video, conduct an on-ground verification and take appropriate action if any violation is established.
